todo_line: - [ ] 004 Implement and test explicit custom-group-removal follow cleanup through public Messaging APIs, including manual and auto-follow sources, idempotent stale-safe remove/re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behaviour.

validation.evidence: 35 tests, 0 failures. Proves generated and historic membership ordering, manual/root/reply follow cleanup facts, first-delivery and later-conversation safety, a suspended-handler remove/re-add/follow race, shared-skip replay, eventual and exact-retry completion, successful execution-result unfollows, lag blocking, and Everyone/Admin no-ops.

41 tests, 0 failures. Proves aggregate generation refresh/cutoffs, delayed stale manual and root-auto follow rejection, absent-field replay, legacy-cleaned first delivery, deterministic follow projections, composed access, and existing send/lag behavior.

notes: Club now assigns a monotonically increasing group-membership generation to add/remove facts; historic absent fields replay by incrementing Club state, while historic Messaging facts normalize to generation zero. Manual follows, root MessageSent auto-follows, and authoritative root-stream reply follows carry the current generation. ConversationFollowers stores per-person follow generations and cleanup cutoffs, refreshes an already-following member after re-add, ignores older first-delivery cleanup, and blocks delayed stale follow work; cleanup IDs remain retry deduplication only. Public custom-group add/remove calls additionally await the cleanup handler's durable EventStore subscription checkpoint after every successful dispatch, including :eventual and event-free retries, while preserving return modes. Focused races cover first delayed delivery, later-created and shared-skipped conversations, legacy cleanup, projection lag, unrelated follows, both system groups, and successful {:ok, result} unfollows. The initial TDD run failed because generation fields were absent; subsequent diagnostic runs exposed one legacy token test whose follow needed an explicitly newer generation. The repository formatter was also checked successfully for every changed Elixir file.
